text:
**Short answer:** For most campers, get a small LiFePO4 unit of about 300Wh. If you want to run a fridge, a CPAP for several nights, or a group's gear, step up to about 1,000Wh. Prices below come from the review sites and may have changed.

**Best picks (from PowerStationGearLab's 2026 camping guide)**

- **Best overall: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus.** It has 288Wh, 300W output and weighs about 8.3 lb, at roughly $249. It's light, simple and easy to recharge from solar. The guide says it can run a CPAP for multiple nights. Jackery's US site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you may find it only at retailers. [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=jackery+explorer+300+plus+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20) (affiliate link)
- **Best value: EcoFlow River 3 Plus.** It has 286Wh (expandable to 572Wh) and 600W output, and weighs about 9.9 lb, at roughly $269–299. It has the same capacity as the Jackery with double the AC power. [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=ecoflow+river+3+plus+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20) (affiliate link)
- **Best for longer trips: Anker SOLIX C300.** It has 288Wh and 300W output at roughly $199. It adds a built-in LED lantern, dual USB-C ports and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the version with AC outlets, not the DC-only one. [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=anker+solix+c300+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20) (affiliate link)
- **Best budget: Bluetti EB3A.** It has 268Wh and 600W output at roughly $179. The app is basic and it's less polished than the others. [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=bluetti+eb3a+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20) (affiliate link)
- **Best for van life, overlanding or a 12V fridge: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2.** It has 1,070Wh and 1,500W output and weighs about 23.8 lb, at roughly $799. [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=jackery+explorer+1000+v2+power+station&tag=pmc0ef-20) (affiliate link)

**Bigger option on sale: Bluetti AC180.** It has 1,152Wh and 1,800W output (4 AC outlets) and weighs about 35 lb. It takes up to 500W of solar input and reaches 80% charge from AC in about 45 minutes.
- Dealectric's page lists it at $499. Code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off, for $474.05 at Bluetti's official US store. That was tested in the cart on 2026-10-21, and checkout sets the final price.
- It has a 5-year warranty if you buy from an official store, and a 30-day return window where you pay return shipping.
- It has no expansion port.
- [Buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link)

**How to choose**
- **Weekend trips with phones, lights and a laptop:** a ~300Wh unit is enough. I'd pick the Anker if you want the lowest price, or the EcoFlow if you want to run a small kettle or fan.
- **CPAP, a fridge or cooking gadgets:** go to roughly 1,000Wh, such as the Jackery 1000 v2 or Bluetti AC180.
- **Solar:** all of these accept solar panels, but you buy the panels separately.

I couldn't open the WIRED and OutdoorGearLab guides, so these picks rest mainly on one review site and the Dealectric listing. I can check other sources or narrow this down if you tell me what you need to power and your budget.
